Suspicious child process spawned during 'npm install' lifecycle hook execution AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for native script/downloader binaries spawned as a descendant of node.exe running an npm install/ci command — the exact 'install-time lifecycle script' code-execution surface GitHub describes as 'the single largest code-execution surface in the npm ecosystem.' Targets compromised preinstall/install/postinstall hooks executing arbitrary code from a transitive dependency. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact framing: 'npm install ... runs scripts from every transitive dependency' via 'preinstall, install, or postinstall' hooks. node.exe + npm-cli.js parent + downloader/script-interpreter child is the literal process tree GitHub is describing as the largest code-execution surface.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1195.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Husky postinstall hook spawning sh/cmd to install git hooks
  • Prisma generate spawning powershell to detect platform binaries
  • electron-builder postinstall pulling platform-specific binaries via curl
  • Internal developer tooling with legitimate postinstall scripts running PowerShell setup
  • CI runner doing npm ci where build steps legitimately spawn cmd.exe wrappers
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("husky install","prisma generate","electron-builder install-app-deps","node-gyp rebuild","esbuild","@swc/core")) and not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("\\node_modules\\husky\\","\\node_modules\\prisma\\","\\node_modules\\electron\\"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Pull the full ProcessCommandLine and parent npm command — identify which package's lifecycle hook is the parent's working directory (look at cwd or InitiatingProcessFolderPath). Open package.json in that directory and check the scripts.preinstall/install/postinstall declarations. 2. Contain: If the package isn't recognised as an organisationally-approved dependency, kill the node.exe process tree, snapshot node_modules/<package>, and isolate the developer host from the network. Rotate any npm registry tokens stored in ~/.npmrc on that host. 3. Hunt: Pivot on the package name across all developer/CI hosts to find other installations; check npm registry audit logs for when this version was first published; review DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound connections from the same child process to flag C2/exfil destinations.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm-cli.js", "npm install", "npm ci", "run-script", "lifecycle", "preinstall", "postinstall")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","regsvr32.exe","rundll32.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("husky","prisma generate","electron-builder","node-gyp rebuild"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "node.exe"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm-cli.js", "npm install", "npm ci", "run-script", "preinstall", "postinstall")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","regsvr32.exe","rundll32.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where not(TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("husky","prisma","electron-builder","node-gyp rebuild"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

npm v12 mitigation bypass via --allow-git, --allow-remote, or script re-enable flags AIWeaponization High
Alerts on npm invocations that explicitly opt out of the new npm v12 hardening — namely --allow-git, --allow-remote, or attempts to re-enable lifecycle scripts via --ignore-scripts=false / NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false / a global allowScripts override. These flags are the exact bypass surface GitHub introduced; their presence in a build or CI command indicates a deliberate downgrade of the default mitigation. Rationale: These flag strings are taken directly from the article — '--allow-git', '--allow-remote', and the existing '--ignore-scripts' flag are named explicitly. Their use in a build pipeline indicates a deliberate downgrade of the new default hardening — exactly the bypass mode an attacker (or careless developer) would invoke post-npm-v12.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal package author legitimately using --allow-git to install from a private GitHub repo dep
  • Developer migrating a legacy build that still requires lifecycle scripts and using --allow-scripts during transition
  • CI pipeline temporarily using NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false to compare pre/post-v12 behavior during the version bump
  • Open-source maintainer testing their own package's install scripts with --foreground-scripts for verbose output
Suppression filter
| where not(DeviceName has_any ("build-trusted-","signing-host-")) and AccountName !in~ ("npm-publish-svc","release-bot")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Identify whether the host is a developer workstation or a CI runner — pull the parent process and the working directory to map this to a specific repo/project. Check git log on the repo for who recently modified package.json, build scripts, or .npmrc. 2. Contain: If this is a CI runner, halt the pipeline and revert the offending commit until reviewed. If a developer workstation, contact the user to confirm intent. 3. Hunt: Search for the same flag use across all CI/dev hosts in the same org over the last 30 days; pull the list of packages installed under that flag from npm-debug logs and cross-reference any new/unfamiliar packages against npm registry publish dates (catch newly-published malicious packages riding through the bypass).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
   or FileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--allow-git", "--allow-remote", "--allow-scripts", "--ignore-scripts=false", "--ignore-scripts false", "--foreground-scripts", "NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false", "NPM_CONFIG_ALLOW_SCRIPTS")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--allow-git", "--allow-remote", "--allow-scripts", "--ignore-scripts=false", "NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm ", "npm.exe", "npm-cli.js", "install", "ci")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm ", "npm-cli.js", "install", "ci")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") or TargetProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("--allow-git", "--allow-remote", "--allow-scripts", "--ignore-scripts=false", "--ignore-scripts false", "--foreground-scripts", "NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false", "NPM_CONFIG_ALLOW_SCRIPTS")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("--allow-git", "--allow-remote", "--allow-scripts", "NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=false")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm-cli.js", "npm install", "npm ci", "npm ")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm-cli.js", "npm install", "npm ci")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious .npmrc dropped inside node_modules to override git executable AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for .npmrc file writes that land inside a node_modules subdirectory — the precise attack the article calls out, where 'a Git dependency's .npmrc configuration file could override the Git executable, even with --ignore-scripts.' A legitimate project .npmrc lives at the repo root or user home, never under node_modules/<package>/. Rationale: The article explicitly names this attack path: 'a Git dependency's .npmrc configuration file used could override the Git executable, even with --ignore-scripts.' A .npmrc nested under node_modules/<package>/ is precisely the file shape that abuses this — legitimate .npmrc lives at repo root or user-home only.
ATT&CKT1574 T1195.001 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually editing a vendored package under node_modules for debugging (rare but legitimate)
  • Yarn berry / pnpm vendoring step that emits .npmrc inside their content-addressed cache under node_modules/.cache/
  • npm pack/unpack operation extracting a package that bundles an .npmrc for legitimate registry config (still suspicious, but lawful)
  • Monorepo tooling like Lerna or Nx writing per-package .npmrc for sub-project registry scoping
Suppression filter
| where not(FolderPath has_any ("\\node_modules\\.cache\\","\\node_modules\\.pnpm\\")) and not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","notepad.exe","notepad++.exe"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Read the .npmrc content and check for git=, script-shell=, ignore-scripts=false, or registry= overrides pointing at unfamiliar hosts. Identify the parent package directory and pull its package.json to learn the package name + version. 2. Contain: If a git/script-shell override is present, kill any running node/git processes for that user, remove the malicious .npmrc, and isolate the workstation/CI runner. Search ~/.npmrc and the user's git config for any inherited overrides too. 3. Hunt: Search ThreatFox / OSV / Socket.dev for the package@version that wrote the file. Pivot on the package name across all node_modules trees in the org; check git history on the affected repo's package-lock.json for when this dependency entered the tree.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ ".npmrc"
| where FolderPath has "\\node_modules\\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","git.exe","tar.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","7z.exe","unzip.exe")
| where not(FolderPath endswith "\\node_modules\\")
| extend PackagePath = extract(@"(?i)\\node_modules\\([^\\]+)", 1, FolderPath)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, PackagePath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc"
| where TargetFilePath has "\\node_modules\\"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","git.exe","tar.exe","npm.exe","7z.exe","unzip.exe")
| extend PackagePath = extract(@"(?i)\\node_modules\\([^\\]+)", 1, TargetFilePath)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, PackagePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: .npmrc Written Inside node_modules Package Directory
id: c4c91e51-3a72-4f1d-8c1f-7a9d6b8f2a13
description: Detects creation of a .npmrc file underneath a node_modules/<package>/ tree. The npm v12 GitHub advisory calls out that a Git dependency's bundled .npmrc can override the git executable even when --ignore-scripts is set; legitimate .npmrc files live at the project root or user home, never beneath node_modules.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.t1574
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\.npmrc'
    TargetFilename|contains: '\node_modules\'
  filter_known_good:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\code.exe'
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\notepad.exe'
      - '\notepad++.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_good
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\.npmrc) @TargetFilename:(*\node_modules\* OR *\Node_Modules\*) @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\git.exe OR *\tar.exe OR *\npm.exe OR *\7z.exe OR *\unzip.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\node_modules\\[^\\]+\\.*\.npmrc$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(node|git|tar|npm|7z|unzip)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\node_modules\\\\(?<pkg>[^\\\\]+)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, pkg, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name=".npmrc" Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\*" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| where NOT match(file_path, "(?i)\\\\node_modules\\\\\\.cache\\\\")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name=".npmrc" Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\*" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| where NOT match(file_path, "(?i)\\\\node_modules\\\\\\.cache\\\\")
Implicit node-gyp rebuild from binding.gyp spawning non-build child process AIInstallation Low
Hunts for the niche execution path the article calls out: 'a package with a binding.gyp and no explicit install script still gets blocked, because npm runs an implicit node-gyp rebuild for it.' A malicious package can carry only a binding.gyp and rely on the implicit rebuild to gain code execution. Legitimate node-gyp builds spawn python.exe/msbuild.exe/cl.exe; anything else from node-gyp is suspicious. Rationale: Quote from article: 'a package with a binding.gyp and no explicit install script still gets blocked, because npm runs an implicit node-gyp rebuild for it.' Allowlisting genuine build toolchain binaries (python, msbuild, cl, link) and flagging anything else from a node-gyp parent surfaces the abusable side of the implicit rebuild path.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom corporate build wrappers that legitimately invoke gyp_python and a vendored toolchain binary not in the allowlist
  • Pre-gyp / prebuildify spawning curl.exe or wget.exe to download platform-specific prebuilt binaries (common for sharp, bcrypt, sqlite3)
  • Yarn workspaces wiring node-gyp via a different node binary path causing the parent match to miss legit children
  • Visual Studio Build Tools auxiliary tooling like rc.exe / midl.exe paths varying across SDK versions
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("sharp","bcrypt","sqlite3","canvas","better-sqlite3","node-sass","sass","@tensorflow","node-rdkafka","node-pty")) and not(FileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "prebuild")
Response runbook
1. Triage: From InitiatingProcessCommandLine, identify the package directory (look for the node_modules/<package> in the cwd or args). Open its package.json — confirm whether 'install' or 'scripts.install' is empty and only a binding.gyp is present (the exact shape the article describes). 2. Contain: Halt the npm install/CI job. Snapshot the package directory and remove the dependency from package.json + package-lock.json. 3. Hunt: Search Socket.dev / npm advisory feed for the package@version; pivot on the package name across all dev/CI hosts; check the binding.gyp content for shell-out actions like 'action': ['<some-binary>', ...] that aren't a clean compile-and-link.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp", "binding.gyp", "node-gyp rebuild", "node-gyp.js")
| where FileName !in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","msbuild.exe","cl.exe","link.exe","node.exe","conhost.exe","cmd.exe","where.exe","vswhere.exe","makensis.exe","git.exe","rc.exe","midl.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "node.exe"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp", "binding.gyp", "node-gyp rebuild", "node-gyp.js")
| where not(TargetProcessName has_any ("\\python.exe","\\python3.exe","\\msbuild.exe","\\cl.exe","\\link.exe","\\node.exe","\\conhost.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\where.exe","\\vswhere.exe","\\git.exe","\\rc.exe","\\midl.exe"))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: node-gyp Implicit Rebuild Spawning Non-Build Child Process
id: e2b8d439-6c4f-49ad-9b07-1d2f0a3e7c92
description: Detects the implicit node-gyp rebuild path the GitHub npm v12 advisory calls out — a package shipping only a binding.gyp triggers node-gyp rebuild and gains arbitrary code execution. Legitimate node-gyp work spawns python.exe, msbuild.exe, cl.exe, link.exe; anything else is suspicious.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/github-to-disable-npm-install-scripts.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/12
tags:

logsource:

      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\where.exe'
      - '\vswhere.exe'
      - '\git.exe'

      - '\midl.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and not filter_legit_build
level: low
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE) @ParentCommandLine:(*node-gyp* OR *binding.gyp* OR *"node-gyp rebuild"*) -@Image:(*\python.exe OR *\python3.exe OR *\msbuild.exe OR *\MSBuild.exe OR *\cl.exe OR *\link.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\conhost.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\where.exe OR *\vswhere.exe OR *\git.exe OR *\rc.exe OR *\midl.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^node\.exe$/i
| ParentCommandLine=/node-gyp|binding\.gyp|node-gyp\s+rebuild/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\(python3?|msbuild|cl|link|node|conhost|cmd|where|vswhere|git|rc|midl)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentCommandLine], function=count())

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="node.exe" (Processes.parent_process="*node-gyp*" OR Processes.parent_process="*binding.gyp*" OR Processes.parent_process="*rebuild*") Processes.process_name!="python.exe" Processes.process_name!="python3.exe" Processes.process_name!="msbuild.exe" Processes.process_name!="cl.exe" Processes.process_name!="link.exe" Processes.process_name!="node.exe" Processes.process_name!="conhost.exe" Processes.process_name!="cmd.exe" Processes.process_name!="where.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)

    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"

            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty

NETWORK

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |

references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 exploitation via /mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage AIExploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated POST/GET requests to the ConfigServiceController endpoint exploited by the public Python PoC for CVE-2026-10520. This endpoint is reached pre-auth on the standard HTTPS listener and is almost never hit by legitimate clients, so any request bearing shell metacharacters or LOLBin tokens in the body/URI is treatable as exploitation. Rationale: The vulnerable endpoint path `/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage` on ConfigServiceController is the high-fidelity article-specific pivot (corroborated via watchTowr Labs, Help Net Security, Rapid7). It is reached pre-auth on the standard HTTPS interface and has effectively zero legitimate hits, so any traffic to it during the exploitation window is treatable as suspicious; we additionally tag requests carrying shell metacharacters or LOLBin tokens. Cross-checked against: • https://labs.watchtowr.com/more-evidence-that-words-dont-mean-what-we-thought-they-meant-ivanti-sentry-pre-auth-os-command-injection-cve-2026-10520/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/10/ivanti-sentry-cve-2026-10520-cve-2026-10523/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2026-10520-cve-2026-10523-multiple-critical-vulnerabilities-affecting-ivanti-sentry/ • https://socradar.io/blog/ivanti-sentrys-cve-2026-10520-rce/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised Ivanti support engineer running internal config probe against /mics/api/v2/ for diagnostics
  • Internal vulnerability scanner (Tenable / Qualys / Rapid7) sending CVE-2026-10520 detection probes from a known scanner subnet
  • Shadowserver or other internet-wide scanner pinging the endpoint without payload (UA 'Shadowserver')
  • Newly added legitimate MICS automation client calling the endpoint with empty body
Suppression filter
| where Src !in ("<shadowserver_ranges>", "<internal_scanner_ips>") and UA !has "Shadowserver" and UA !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","InsightVM")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full HTTP transaction (URI + body if WAF captures it). Confirm caller IP is not in the scanner/Shadowserver allow-list, check Sentry version against R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1, and review tomcat/catalina logs for the same request ID. 2) Contain: temporarily block the caller IP at perimeter, isolate the Sentry appliance from internal back-ends (Exchange/ActiveSync), and snapshot the filesystem before any reboot. 3) Hunt: review the appliance's last 30 days of syslog for root-level shell spawns from the tomcat user, any new SSH keys under /home/* or /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, new cron entries, and outbound connections to non-Ivanti destinations.
// Defender rarely sees inbound WAF traffic to a Linux appliance; this pivots on the compromised Sentry calling back outbound from MDE-instrumented neighbours
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let VulnPath = "/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage";
let ShellMeta = dynamic([";","|","&","`","$(","%3B","%7C","%26","%60","%24%28"]);
let LolBin = dynamic(["curl","wget","bash","/bin/sh"," nc ","chmod","/tmp/","/dev/tcp/","python -c","perl -e"]);
union isfuzzy=true
 (CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has VulnPath or Message has VulnPath
  | extend Url = coalesce(RequestURL, Message), Method = RequestMethod, Src = SourceIP, Dst = DestinationIP, UA = RequestClientApplication),
 (W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriStem has VulnPath
  | extend Url = strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), Method = csMethod, Src = cIP, Dst = Computer, UA = csUserAgent)
| extend InjHit = iff(Url has_any (ShellMeta) or Url has_any (LolBin), "true", "false")
| project TimeGenerated, Src, Dst, Method, Url, UA, InjHit
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 ConfigServiceController Exploitation
id: 9e2c41d6-7b3a-4a5b-9c4e-21f6d8a01520
description: Detects pre-auth POST/GET requests to the ConfigServiceController handleMessage endpoint exploited by the public PoC for CVE-2026-10520 in Ivanti Sentry (MobileIron Sentry).
references:
  - https://labs.watchtowr.com/more-evidence-that-words-dont-mean-what-we-thought-they-meant-ivanti-sentry-pre-auth-os-command-injection-cve-2026-10520/
  - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/10/ivanti-sentry-cve-2026-10520-cve-2026-10523/
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/max-severity-ivanti-sentry-vulnerability-now-exploited-in-attacks/
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.004
  - cve.2026.10520
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection_uri:
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage'
  selection_payload:
    cs-uri-query|contains:
      - ';'
      - '|'
      - '`'
      - '$('
      - 'curl '
      - 'wget '
      - '/bin/'
      - 'bash'
      - '/tmp/'
      - '/dev/tcp/'
      - 'chmod'
  condition: selection_uri and (selection_payload or 1 of selection_uri*)
level: high
(source:(nginx OR apache OR azure.applicationgateway OR aws.alb OR cloudflare OR waf) OR @evt.name:HTTPRequest) (@http.url_details.path:*/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage* OR @http.uri:*/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage*)
# log group: /aws/applicationelb (or AWS WAF / CloudFront log group fronting the Sentry appliance)
fields @timestamp, client_ip, target_status_code, request_verb, request_url, user_agent
| filter request_url like /\/mics\/api\/v2\/sentry\/mics-config\/handleMessage/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200

| eval injection_hit=if(match(url,"(?i)(%3B|%7C|%26|%24%28|%60|;|\||&|`|\$\(|/bin/|bash|sh\s|nc\s|curl\s|wget\s|chmod|/tmp/|/dev/tcp/)"),1,0)
| where injection_hit=1 OR isnotnull(url)

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.http_method) as methods values(Web.http_user_agent) as ua values(Web.status) as status from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*/mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage*" by Web.src Web.dest Web.url

| where injection_hit=1 OR isnotnull(url)

Root-level child process spawned by Ivanti Sentry tomcat web user (post-CVE-2026-10520 RCE) AIInstallation High
Hunts shell / LOLBin children spawned by the Sentry appliance's tomcat/web service account (typically running as root or escalating to root). The CVE-2026-10520 PoC achieves root-level OS command execution via injection into ConfigServiceController, so the first observable post-exploit signal on the appliance is a non-Java child of the tomcat JVM running curl/wget/bash/nc. Rationale: The article and corroborating watchTowr/Rapid7 advisories state CVE-2026-10520 enables root-level OS command execution on the Sentry gateway. The Sentry web tier is a Java/Tomcat application — a shell/LOLBin child of catalina.sh or the java process running as root is the canonical post-exploit signal. We anchor on parent=java/catalina.sh + child=shell/network-LOLBin + user=root for high precision. Cross-checked against: • https://labs.watchtowr.com/more-evidence-that-words-dont-mean-what-we-thought-they-meant-ivanti-sentry-pre-auth-os-command-injection-cve-2026-10520/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2026-10520-cve-2026-10523-multiple-critical-vulnerabilities-affecting-ivanti-sentry/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190 T1548
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ivanti-supplied appliance patch / upgrade script invoking bash from a Java-based installer
  • Tomcat startup wrapper (catalina.sh) executing `id`/`whoami` for self-check during boot
  • Authorised SE running diagnostics via the Sentry console that triggers a shell-out
  • Internal config-management tool (Ansible/Salt) executing remote bash steps under the tomcat user
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("/opt/ivanti/","sentry-install","sentry-upgrade") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "/opt/ivanti/sentry/bin/"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full command line for the child process and walk back the parent JVM PID; correlate the same host within ±5 min against UC1 (WAF hits on /mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage). 2) Contain: isolate the Sentry appliance from production network (block egress at firewall, leave management VPN for forensics), suspend its back-end Exchange/ActiveSync connector. 3) Hunt: enumerate /root, /home, /etc/cron.*, /etc/systemd/system, and /tmp for files written by the tomcat user; pull bash_history for root/tomcat; review outbound NetFlow from the appliance for any non-Ivanti destination over the past 30 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","tomcat","catalina.sh")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("catalina","tomcat","sentry")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","id","whoami","uname","chmod")
| where AccountName in~ ("root","tomcat","sentry","mi")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("java","tomcat","catalina.sh")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("catalina","tomcat","sentry")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","python","python3","perl","id","whoami","uname","chmod")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("root","tomcat","sentry","mi")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ivanti Sentry post-exploitation persistence: SSH key, cron, or systemd backdoor AIInstallation Medium
Hunts persistence artefacts written on the Sentry appliance after CVE-2026-10520 exploitation — additions to root/admin authorized_keys, new entries in /etc/cron.*, or new unit files in /etc/systemd/system written by the tomcat/sentry user. Shadowserver confirmed that most exposed instances were backdoored within 24 h of the patch, so persistence is the highest-value secondary signal once UC1/UC2 are silent. Rationale: Article states Shadowserver confirmed Sentry gateways were backdoored within 24 h of patch release. Public Linux-appliance backdoors of this flavour overwhelmingly use authorized_keys / cron / systemd persistence. We anchor on the standard persistence paths plus the constrained set of users that should ever write them on a Sentry appliance (root/tomcat/sentry/mi). Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/max-severity-ivanti-sentry-vulnerability-now-exploited-in-attacks/ • https://securityaffairs.com/193530/uncategorized/cve-2026-10520-exploited-ivanti-sentry-gateways-compromised-shortly-after-patch-release.html • https://socradar.io/blog/ivanti-sentrys-cve-2026-10520-rce/
ATT&CKT1098.004 T1053.003 T1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ivanti-supplied patch installer (R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1) writing a new systemd unit during upgrade
  • Authorised admin rotating root SSH keys post-incident as part of hardening
  • Configuration management (Ansible/Salt/Chef) pushing a scheduled job to the appliance
  • Sentry appliance built-in log-rotation cron entries being updated by a package upgrade
Suppression filter
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("sentry-install","sentry-upgrade","/opt/ivanti/sentry/bin/","yum ","dnf ","apt ","rpm -")
Response runbook
1) Triage: diff the file against the last known-good copy (or vendor's reference image) — pull the public-key fingerprint or cron payload. Verify whether the modifying process was a vendor patch installer (correlate to recorded change-management). 2) Contain: revert the file to a clean copy, terminate any active SSH sessions for the affected account, force-rotate root and service-account credentials, snapshot the disk for forensics before any reboot. 3) Hunt: pivot on the cron payload / SSH key fingerprint across the rest of the appliance fleet and across other Ivanti products in the estate; review outbound connections from the appliance for the past 30 days for any beaconing pattern.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/root/.ssh/","/.ssh/authorized_keys","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/cron.hourly/","/etc/cron.daily/","/var/spool/cron/","/etc/systemd/system/","/etc/crontab")
   or FileName in~ ("authorized_keys","crontab")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("root","tomcat","sentry","mi")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java","bash","sh","sed","tee","echo","cp","mv")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/root/.ssh/","/.ssh/authorized_keys","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/cron.hourly/","/etc/cron.daily/","/var/spool/cron/","/etc/systemd/system/","/etc/crontab")
   or TargetFileName in~ ("authorized_keys","crontab")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("root","tomcat","sentry","mi")
   or ActingProcessName has_any ("java","bash","sh","tee","sed","echo")

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Ivanti Sentry version inventory (CVE-2026-10520 / CVE-2026-10523 exposure) AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt that surfaces all hosts in the estate still running an Ivanti Sentry version vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 / CVE-2026-10523 — i.e. anything below R10.5.2, R10.6.2 or R10.7.1. Given Shadowserver's assertion that 'if you have not patched now you are most likely compromised', this query feeds the patching backlog and the proactive compromise-assessment scope. Rationale: Article explicitly names patched versions R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1 and warns that unpatched instances are most likely already compromised. The Defender/Sentinel TVM tables index by CveId, so a direct lookup on CVE-2026-10520 / CVE-2026-10523 returns the entire estate's exposure list. Joining against DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing prioritises the highest-risk subset (the population Shadowserver was scanning). Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/max-severity-ivanti-sentry-vulnerability-now-exploited-in-attacks/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/10/ivanti-sentry-cve-2026-10520-cve-2026-10523/ • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-cve-2026-10520-cve-2026-10523-multiple-critical-vulnerabilities-affecting-ivanti-sentry/
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Decommissioned Sentry appliance still in CMDB but powered off
  • Lab / non-production Sentry instance behind an air-gapped network
  • TVM signature lag — host actually patched in the last 24 h but inventory not yet refreshed
  • Sentry appliance whose admin interface is not reachable by the scanner (false negative, not FP — flag for manual review)
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each returned host, confirm the current installed version via the Sentry admin interface (or vendor-provided CLI) and verify IsInternetFacing against perimeter firewall rules. 2) Contain: schedule emergency patching to R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1; for internet-exposed instances that cannot be patched immediately, restrict /mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage at the perimeter WAF/reverse-proxy. 3) Hunt: run UC1, UC2, UC3 against the same host list for the past 30 days to compromise-assess every vulnerable instance — Shadowserver's guidance is to assume unpatched + exposed = compromised.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-10520","CVE-2026-10523")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-10520","CVE-2026-10523")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, OSPlatform) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
| inputlookup cmdb_assets.csv
| search software_vendor="Ivanti" AND (software_name="Sentry" OR software_name="MobileIron Sentry")
| eval major=mvindex(split(software_version,"."),0), minor=mvindex(split(software_version,"."),1), patch=mvindex(split(software_version,"."),2)
| eval vulnerable=case(
    software_version IN ("10.5.0","10.5.1"), "CVE-2026-10520 (fix R10.5.2)",
    software_version IN ("10.6.0","10.6.1"), "CVE-2026-10520 (fix R10.6.2)",
    software_version IN ("10.7.0"), "CVE-2026-10520 (fix R10.7.1)",
    1=1, "check")
| where vulnerable!="check"
| table host ip software_name software_version vulnerable last_seen

// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High

| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-10520 — Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-06-11 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution. This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors. Vendor: Ivanti, Product: Sentry. Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Vulnerable Langflow versions present in estate (CVE-2026-5027 exposure) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Langflow CVE-2026-5027 exploit chain: /api/v1/auto_login token then POST /api/v2/files · [LLM] Langflow worker spawns shell or LOLBin child (CVE-2026-5027 RCE)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Langflow Python process writes file outside data dir (CVE-2026-5027 post-exploit drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Langflow CVE-2026-5027 exploit chain: /api/v1/auto_login token then POST /api/v2/files AIExploitation High
Detects the documented exploitation pattern for CVE-2026-5027 where an unauthenticated attacker first hits Langflow's auto-login endpoint to mint a session token, then within seconds POSTs to /api/v2/files to write an arbitrary file via the unsanitised filename multipart parameter. Correlating both URIs from the same source IP within a tight window is far higher fidelity than alerting on either endpoint individually. Rationale: Article explicitly names both URIs (POST /api/v2/files for the traversal, plus the unauthenticated auto-login step that mints the session token in 'a single unauthenticated request'). Pairing them in a same-source-IP / same-host time-window correlation eliminates the noise of either endpoint hit alone. Tenable TRA-2026-26 and the public PoC (github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027) both confirm the two-step pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html • https://www.securityweek.com/hackers-exploit-langflow-vulnerability-for-remote-code-execution/ • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) probing the auto_login + file upload endpoints during authenticated scans
  • Langflow integration tests / CI pipelines that exercise the auto_login + file upload flow against a staging instance
  • Developer demo flows where a single user logs in and immediately uploads a flow JSON
  • Bug-bounty researchers / red-team engagements pre-notified to the SOC
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("<scanner_ip_1>","<scanner_ip_2>") | where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Rapid7","InsightVM")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the SrcIpAddr's geo and reputation, the User-Agent string, and the HTTP response code for the /api/v2/files POST (200 = file written, 403 = blocked). If response is 200, treat as confirmed compromise. 2) Contain: take the Langflow instance offline or front it with a WAF rule blocking POST /api/v2/files where filename contains '../'; rotate any secrets reachable from the Langflow host (API keys, OpenAI tokens, MCP creds). 3) Hunt: pivot on the destination host's DeviceFileEvents/FileWritten for files written by python/uvicorn outside the Langflow data dir (UC2), and check the host's process tree (UC3) for shells spawned from the langflow process. Confirm version is <1.9.0 (UC4) and upgrade to 1.10.0.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSec = 120s;
let TokenHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | where Url has "/api/v1/auto_login"
    | project TokenTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "/api/v2/files"
| project UploadTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| join kind=inner TokenHits on SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr
| where UploadTime between (TokenTime .. TokenTime + WindowSec)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', UploadTime, TokenTime)
| project TokenTime, UploadTime, DelaySec, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by UploadTime desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:azure.appservice) @http.method:POST @http.url_details.path:("/api/v1/auto_login" OR "/api/v2/files")
WEB

| tstats summariesonly=true earliest(_time) as token_time from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST AND Web.uri_path="*/api/v1/auto_login*" by Web.src, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename src as exploit_src dest as target_host | join type=inner exploit_src target_host [ | tstats summariesonly=true earliest(_time) as upload_time values(Web.uri_path) as upload_paths values(Web.status) as upload_statuses values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST AND Web.uri_path="*/api/v2/files*" by Web.src, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename src as exploit_src dest as target_host ] | eval delay_sec=upload_time - token_time | where delay_sec >= 0 AND delay_sec <= 120 | table exploit_src, target_host, token_time, upload_time, delay_sec, upload_paths, upload_statuses, user_agents | sort - upload_time
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) as token_time from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST AND Web.uri_path="*/api/v1/auto_login*" by Web.src, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename src as exploit_src dest as target_host | join type=inner exploit_src target_host [ | tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) as upload_time values(Web.uri_path) as upload_paths values(Web.status) as upload_statuses values(Web.http_user_agent) as user_agents from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.http_method=POST AND Web.uri_path="*/api/v2/files*" by Web.src, Web.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename src as exploit_src dest as target_host ] | eval delay_sec=upload_time - token_time | where delay_sec >= 0 AND delay_sec <= 120 | table exploit_src, target_host, token_time, upload_time, delay_sec, upload_paths, upload_statuses, user_agents | sort - upload_time
Langflow Python process writes file outside data dir (CVE-2026-5027 post-exploit drop) AIInstallation High
Once the path-traversal write succeeds, the Langflow worker (python/uvicorn/gunicorn) is the process that writes the attacker-controlled file. Hunts for files written by that process to high-value system paths or with extensions/names indicating webshells, cron persistence, or SSH key implantation. Catches the post-exploit drop even when web/WAF logs aren't ingested. Rationale: Article confirms the impact is 'write arbitrary files on exposed servers' and VulnCheck honeypots observed 'test files' being dropped. The Langflow worker process is the only legitimate writer to its data directory, so a write by that process to /etc/, web roots, SSH key files, or cron from this process is the clean exploit indicator. Avoids false-positives on legitimate flow saves by anchoring on path/extension rather than just process identity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1098.004 T1053.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Langflow legitimately writing user-uploaded flow JSON or RAG corpus files to a non-standard data directory configured via LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR
  • Langflow component that writes logs to /var/log via a custom logging handler
  • Python pip install/upgrade of Langflow plugins writing into site-packages (often under /usr/local/lib/python*/)
  • Backup/sync tools running as the langflow service user touching shared paths
  • Custom-flow component using python-shell or os.system to legitimately write artefacts
Suppression filter
| where not (TargetFilePath has "site-packages" and TargetFileName endswith ".py") | where ActorUsername != "root" or TargetFilePath !startswith "/var/log/langflow"
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash the dropped file and check VT/Defender verdict; examine the file content directly (cat the .php / .sh / authorized_keys) for webshell magic strings or attacker SSH keys. Cross-reference Timestamp with web-log POSTs to /api/v2/files (UC1) from external IPs within ±2 minutes. 2) Contain: quarantine the file, kill the Langflow worker process, rotate the service account, remove any added SSH keys / cron entries / WAR files, and block the source IP at the perimeter. 3) Hunt: pivot on DeviceProcessEvents for any child process spawned by the langflow worker (UC3); look for outbound connections from the langflow process to non-RFC1918 IPs in DeviceNetworkEvents in the prior 24h.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ExpectedDataPaths = pack_array(@"\langflow\", @"\.langflow\", @"\langflow_data\", "/langflow/", "/.langflow/", "/langflow_data/", "/var/lib/langflow", "/tmp/langflow");
let SuspiciousPaths = pack_array("/etc/", "/root/", "/var/www/", "/var/spool/cron/", "/usr/local/bin/", "/.ssh/", @"\Windows\", @"\System32\", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\", @"\Startup\", @"\ProgramData\");
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn","langflow")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","langflow_backend","-m langflow")
| where not(FolderPath has_any (ExpectedDataPaths))
| where FolderPath has_any (SuspiciousPaths)
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)(authorized_keys|crontab|sudoers|webshell|\.php$|\.jsp$|\.aspx$|\.sh$)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let ExpectedDataPaths = dynamic([@"\langflow\", "/langflow/", "/.langflow/", "/langflow_data/", "/var/lib/langflow"]);
let SuspiciousPaths = dynamic(["/etc/", "/root/", "/var/www/", "/var/spool/cron/", "/usr/local/bin/", "/.ssh/", @"\Windows\", @"\System32\", @"\inetpub\wwwroot\", @"\Startup\"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated" or EventType =~ "FileModified"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","uvicorn","gunicorn","langflow")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow")
| where not(TargetFilePath has_any (ExpectedDataPaths))
| where TargetFilePath has_any (SuspiciousPaths)
   or TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)(authorized_keys|crontab|sudoers|webshell|\.php$|\.jsp$|\.aspx$|\.sh$)"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Langflow worker spawns shell or LOLBin child (CVE-2026-5027 RCE) AIExploitation High
Path-traversal-to-RCE on Langflow typically ends with the python/uvicorn worker spawning a shell (bash/sh/cmd) or download utility (curl/wget) to fetch a second-stage payload after the implant lands. Detects any non-python child of the langflow worker process — Langflow legitimately runs sub-pythons only. Rationale: Tenable's TRA-2026-26 and the public PoC both demonstrate the path traversal escalating to RCE by writing an executable file the langflow worker later invokes — or by the upload handler triggering interpreter execution. Langflow's worker should only ever spawn other python interpreters (subprocess pools); a bash/curl/wget child of the langflow worker is a strong RCE indicator. Anchoring on parent cmdline containing 'langflow' avoids FPs from arbitrary python scripts on the box. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027 • https://www.securityweek.com/hackers-exploit-langflow-vulnerability-for-remote-code-execution/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.003 T1190 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom Langflow component that legitimately shells out (e.g. a flow node that runs a local CLI tool — git, ffmpeg, pandoc)
  • Langflow startup script using bash to source env vars or do tini-style init
  • Healthcheck probes that exec curl from the Langflow container to test connectivity
  • Developer using `langflow run` interactively in a terminal where the parent shell is recorded as parent of python
  • Backup component shelling out to tar/gzip from within a flow
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "healthcheck" and ProcessCommandLine !has "--version" | where not (FileName in~ ("curl","wget") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("pypi.org","files.pythonhosted.org","huggingface.co"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: examine the ProcessCommandLine — look for base64 blobs, IPs/URLs being fetched, or output redirection to /tmp/.X paths. Pull the SHA256 of any downloaded file and check VT. 2) Contain: kill the Langflow process tree, snapshot the host, isolate via Defender or EDR isolation. Pull memory if a payload is likely in-memory only. 3) Hunt: identify all hosts running Langflow <1.9.0 (UC4) and check each for the same parent-child shape in the prior 14 days; pivot on outbound DeviceNetworkEvents from the langflow worker for any non-pip/non-PyPI destinations.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","perl","ruby")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","chmod +x","/tmp/.","wget http","curl -o","socket.socket")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","perl","ruby")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","chmod +x","/tmp/.","wget http","curl -o")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, MD5, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Langflow versions present in estate (CVE-2026-5027 exposure) AIReconnaissance High
Asset-hunting query to surface every host running Langflow <1.9.0 (or langflow-base <0.8.3) — the versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-5027 and the related Langflow CVEs (CVE-2026-0770, CVE-2026-21445, CVE-2026-33017, CVE-2025-3248). Combines Defender TVM data with live process telemetry because pip-installed Langflow may not always be in the software inventory. Rationale: Article specifies the exact version boundaries: langflow-base <0.8.3 and Langflow <1.9.0 vulnerable; 1.10.0 is the latest. Cross-checked Tenable TRA-2026-26 and Snyk advisory. ~7,000 publicly-exposed instances per Censys means most orgs running it likely have unpatched copies — making asset discovery the first defensive priority. Combining TVM CveId lookup with live process telemetry covers both inventoried installs and shadow-IT pip installs that TVM may miss. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A test/staging Langflow instance intentionally pinned to an older version for regression testing
  • Air-gapped Langflow instance that doesn't reach the public internet (still worth patching but lower priority)
  • A Langflow fork or downstream redistribution that carries vendor backports of the fix without bumping the version string
  • DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities lag — recently-patched hosts may still show as vulnerable for up to 24h after KB sync
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the version observed by SSH'ing to a sample host and running `langflow --version` or `pip show langflow`. 2) Contain: for any exposed (internet-facing) instance, immediately gate behind a WAF or VPN, disable LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN by setting LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, and enforce LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER. 3) Hunt: for every vulnerable host in the list, run UC1 (web log chain), UC2 (file write), and UC3 (process spawn) against the last 30 days to confirm none have already been exploited; prioritise upgrade to 1.10.0.
let VulnerableLangflowCves = pack_array("CVE-2026-5027","CVE-2026-0770","CVE-2026-21445","CVE-2026-33017","CVE-2025-3248");
let TvmHits = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where CveId in (VulnerableLangflowCves)
       or (SoftwareName has "langflow" and SoftwareVersion matches regex @"^(0\.|1\.[0-8]\.)")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, Source = "TVM";
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
    | summarize Timestamp = max(Timestamp), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceId, DeviceName
    | extend SoftwareName = "langflow (process-observed)", SoftwareVersion = "unknown", CveId = "CVE-2026-5027", VulnerabilitySeverityLevel = "High", SoftwareVendor = "langflow-ai", Source = "Process";
union TvmHits, ProcHits
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, Source
| order by Timestamp desc

Miasma dead-man switch — `rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents` from systemd user service or launchd AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the exact destructive command the Miasma worm runs when its stolen GitHub token is revoked. The dead-man switch is wired to a systemd user service (Linux) or a LaunchAgent (macOS), so the recursive home-directory wipe is spawned from PID 1 / launchd rather than an interactive shell — a parent-process shape that legitimate user `rm` activity almost never produces. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim code block from the article (`rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents`) plus the article's explicit parent context (systemd user service on Linux, LaunchAgent on macOS). Corroborated against Microsoft, JFrog and Phoenix Security reporting on the Shai-Hulud predecessor's identical mechanism. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/ • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again/ • https://phoenix.security/sha1-hulud-shai-hulud-worm-analysis-persistence-iocs/
ATT&CKT1485 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer-authored systemd user timer that genuinely cleans up `~/Cache` or `~/tmp` on a schedule
  • macOS LaunchAgent installed by a backup tool that recursively prunes a staging directory
  • `rm -rf` invoked from a CI runner started via `systemd-run --user` (shape matches but cmdline targets the workspace, not ~)
  • Distro upgrade scripts that fire from systemd and clean stale user caches
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/","/var/cache/","~/Cache","~/.cache","/workspace","/builds/"))
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full ParentCmd and `systemctl --user list-units` / `launchctl list` on the host; identify which .service or .plist file declared this ExecStart and when it was created. Contain: kill the parent service (`systemctl --user stop <unit>` / `launchctl unload <plist>`), snapshot the host before anything else writes to it, force-rotate the user's GitHub PAT and any cloud tokens issued from this workstation. Hunt: pivot on the parent unit's binary hash across the fleet, search `DeviceFileEvents` for the .service/.plist creation event (UC2), and check `~/.config/gh/`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.ssh/` access in the prior 72 hours.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceInfo has_any ("Linux","macOS") or FileName =~ "rm"
| where FileName =~ "rm"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("~/","$HOME","~/Documents")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemd","launchd","launchctl","init")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("systemd","launchd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandparentName = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "/rm" or ActingProcessName == "rm"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "-rf"
  and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("~/","$HOME","~/Documents")
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("systemd","launchd","launchctl","init")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("systemd --user","launchd")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Systemd user service or LaunchAgent dropped by node / npm / pip / gem AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the Miasma persistence primitive: a `~/.config/systemd/user/*.service` (Linux) or `~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist` (macOS) file written by a package-manager or scripting-language child process. The article specifies a 72-hour active monitor installed via these mechanisms — high-signal because legitimate dev tooling rarely writes user-scope autostart units. Rationale: Maps to the article's exact persistence statement: "runs as a systemd user service on Linux or a LaunchAgent on macOS". Narrows on writers (package managers and scripting runtimes) because Miasma is dropped via trojanized npm/PyPI/RubyGems packages and its loader is JavaScript-based per SafeDep's pipeline analysis. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/06/02/preinstall-persistence-inside-red-hat-npm-miasma-credential-stealing-campaign/
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1543.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Snap / Flatpak installers writing user systemd units
  • VS Code Remote Tunnels installing a user LaunchAgent for `code tunnel`
  • Docker Desktop helper writing `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.docker.helper.plist`
  • Genuine Python pipx app installing a user systemd unit for a long-running daemon
  • ngrok / cloudflared installer creating an autostart entry
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("snap install","flatpak install","pipx install","vscode-server","com.docker.","cloudflared install","ngrok service install"))
Response runbook
Triage: read the dropped .service/.plist — extract ExecStart / ProgramArguments and the binary it points to. If it shells out to node/curl/python with an inline base64 or fetches from api.github.com, treat as confirmed. Contain: disable the unit (`systemctl --user disable --now <unit>` / `launchctl unload <plist>`), delete the file, kill the running monitor process, rotate the developer's GitHub PAT and any AWS/GCP/Azure CLI credentials. Hunt: search DeviceProcessEvents for the monitor binary across the fleet, pivot on its hash, and cross-reference UC1 (rm -rf) for hosts where the dead-man switch already fired.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user/" and FileName endswith ".service")

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","bun","python","python3","pip","pip3","ruby","gem","sh","bash","zsh","curl","wget")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user/" and TargetFileName endswith ".service")
   or (TargetFilePath has "/Library/LaunchAgents/" and TargetFileName endswith ".plist")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","bun","python","pip","ruby","gem","sh","bash","zsh","curl","wget")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Miasma AI tool config poisoning — writes to Claude / Cursor / Copilot / Gemini / Kiro / Cline configs AIInstallation Medium
Hunts modification of AI coding-assistant configuration files by a non-IDE process. The article calls out poisoning of Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro and Cline configs as a Miasma capability — backdooring these files lets the worm inject malicious instructions into every future AI-assisted code-gen session, propagating the attack with developer help. Rationale: Anchors on the exact AI-tool list named in the article: "poison configurations of AI coding tools such as Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, and Cline". Filters to package-manager/scripting writers because the worm rides into the dev workstation via trojanized packages, then excludes the legitimate IDE/agent binaries that normally own these files. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/miasma-worm-ai-coding-agent-config-injection/ • https://safedep.io/inside-the-miasma-supply-chain-attack-toolkit/
ATT&CKT1554 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer's own postinstall script that legitimately seeds a `CLAUDE.md` or `.cursorrules` for the repo
  • `npm run setup` that templates `cline_mcp_settings.json` for the team
  • Dotfiles installer (chezmoi, stow, yadm) writing AI configs on fresh laptop
  • Custom `.zshrc` snippet that `tee`s a token into `~/.config/github-copilot/`
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("chezmoi apply","stow ","yadm "," dotfiles","setup-dev-env"))
Response runbook
Triage: diff the written file against the version-controlled dotfile baseline; look for added system prompts that fetch from URLs, run shell commands, or instruct the agent to commit/publish. Contain: revert the file from git or the user's known-good backup, revoke the AI tool's session token / MCP credentials, rotate the developer's GitHub PAT. Hunt: pivot on the writer process hash, check DeviceProcessEvents for the same binary on other dev workstations, and review the user's recent npm/pip installs for trojanized packages.
let ai_tool_paths = dynamic(["/.claude/","/.config/claude/","/.cursor/","/.cursor-tutor/","/.config/github-copilot/","/.config/copilot/","/.gemini/","/.config/gemini/","/.kiro/","/.cline/","/.config/cline/"]);

let legit_writers = dynamic(["code","Code","cursor","Cursor","claude","Claude","gemini","Gemini","copilot","electron","idea","pycharm","Slack"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any (ai_tool_paths)) or (FileName in (ai_tool_files))
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (legit_writers))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","bun","python","python3","pip","ruby","gem","sh","bash","zsh","curl","wget","tee")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
